title: Signature Kind-Chat Code
body:
The Signature Kind-Chat Code is Manon's original design for children's first chat rules, written as a code children can recite. The code's lines are: kind words, private details kept, no hidden-app moves, and tell an adult when a chat feels strange. Its premise is that a code a child can say back is a code a child can follow, and that positive rules, stating what to do, beat lists of bans a child cannot act on.

The design exists because children follow rules they own, and they own rules they can recite.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature kind-chat code for children. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Recite the code together: kind words, private details, no hidden moves, tell an adult
  2. Practice kind disagreement in a game chat
  3. Practice refusing a hidden-app move politely
  4. Practice telling an adult about a strange chat
  5. Post the code where the child plays, in the child's own handwriting where possible

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Code recited together; OK :: Kind disagreement practiced; OK :: Hidden-move refusal practiced; OK :: Tell-an-adult practiced; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The code is a teaching design for younger children, and it must grow with the child, which later designs cover. It does not replace adult supervision for young children. A common mistake is teaching the code once and never practicing it, so it fades before it is needed. title: Signature Private-Details Vault
body:
The Signature Private-Details Vault is Manon's original design for teaching children that personal details belong in a vault, not in conversation. The vault's contents are named together: name, school, address, phone, and schedule, and the vault's rule is that details leave only with a parent's key, meaning a parent's agreement. Its premise is that a vault is easier for a child to imagine than an abstract idea like privacy.

The design treats imagination as the teaching tool: a child who pictures a vault guards its contents.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature private-details vault for children. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Name the vault's contents together
  2. Practice spotting vault details in sample posts
  3. Practice refusing friendly questions that ask for vault details
  4. Check photos for vault details before sharing
  5. Tell an adult when someone keeps asking for vault details

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Vault contents named; OK :: Details spotted in samples; OK :: Refusal practiced; OK :: Photos checked; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The vault is a teaching image, not a technical control, and it does not cover data collected by services themselves. Its goal is a child who chooses privacy, not a child who is merely watched. A common mistake is teaching the vault as a secret to be ashamed of, rather than a treasure to be guarded proudly. title: Signature Photo Pause
body:
The Signature Photo Pause is Manon's original design for a pause before any photo or video is shared by a child. The pause asks three questions: who is in it, what does the background show, and who will see it. Its premise is that sharing is an impulse and a pause is a choice, and the design inserts the choice at exactly the moment the impulse acts.

The design exists because a photo shared in a second can reveal what words would take paragraphs to say.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature photo-sharing pause for children. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Pause before sharing any photo or video
  2. Ask who is in it
  3. Check the background for signs, numbers, and uniforms
  4. Ask permission from everyone pictured
  5. Share only with the agreed audience

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Pause taken before sharing; OK :: People checked; OK :: Background checked; OK :: Permission asked; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The pause is a habit, not a filter, and it cannot recall copies once published. It covers children's own sharing, not adults' sharing of children's images, which carries its own responsibilities. A common mistake is checking after posting, when copies may already exist. title: Signature Stranger-Contact Rule
body:
The Signature Stranger-Contact Rule is Manon's original design for a rule with no judgment in it: stop, save, tell. When a stranger contacts a child or asks personal questions, the child stops replying, saves the message, and tells a trusted adult, every time, without first deciding whether the stranger seems nice. Its premise is that friendliness is free online and therefore cannot be the test.

The design removes judgment from the moment, because judgment is exactly what friendliness is designed to defeat.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature stranger-contact rule for children. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Stop replying at the first personal question
  2. Share no personal details, photos, or location
  3. Save the message with the sender visible
  4. Tell a trusted adult at once
  5. Block only after saving, so evidence is kept

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Reply stopped; OK :: No details shared; OK :: Message saved; OK :: Adult told at once; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The rule is a defensive response, not an investigation: children must never continue a conversation to gather information. Threatening or persistent contact needs prompt adult, service, and where appropriate authority involvement. A common mistake is judging whether a stranger seems nice before deciding what to do. title: Signature Screen-Time Pact
body:
The Signature Screen-Time Pact is Manon's original design for a pact, not a ban: parents and children agree device-free times, overnight charging places, homework before entertainment, and calm consequences stated in advance, and adults keep the pact in spirit too. Its premise is that limits children helped write are limits children keep, while limits imposed without warning are limits children work around.

The design treats agreement as the mechanism, because a pact kept willingly beats a ban enforced resentfully.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature family screen-time pact. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Agree device-free times together
  2. Agree overnight charging outside bedrooms
  3. Agree homework before entertainment
  4. State consequences calmly in advance
  5. Review the pact each school term

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Device-free times agreed; OK :: Charging place agreed; OK :: Homework-first agreed; OK :: Consequences stated in advance; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The pact is a family agreement, not a prescription of hours, since homework, creative work, and calls differ from passive scrolling. Where use becomes compulsive, professional guidance should be sought. A common mistake is writing a pact for children only while adults ignore it themselves. title: Signature Upset-Content Button
body:
The Signature Upset-Content Button is Manon's original design for a response a child can press in their head: close, do not share, tell. The button's rule is that seeing something upsetting is never the child's fault and never something to hide, and the adult's response to the telling must be calm and grateful, so the child tells again next time. Its premise is that the first adult response decides every later report.

The design exists because a child who is punished for telling will simply stop telling.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature upset-content response for children. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Close the upsetting page or app
  2. Do not share the content onward
  3. Tell a trusted adult and show what was seen
  4. Use the report button together
  5. Talk about it in plain words, without blame

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Page closed; OK :: Content not shared onward; OK :: Adult told; OK :: Report used together; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The button covers ordinary upsetting content, not illegal or abusive material, which adults must report through proper channels and must never ask a child to handle. It does not replace professional support where a child is distressed. A common mistake is punishing a child for seeing upsetting content. title: Signature Game-Chat Guard
body:
The Signature Game-Chat Guard is Manon's original design for gaming: known friends by default, new friends confirmed with an adult, no cross-app gifts or trades, and abusive chat muted without reply. Its premise is that games make strangers feel like teammates within minutes, so the guard must be set before play starts, not during it.

The design treats a game's friend list as a door, and doors need locks before guests arrive.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature gaming chat guard. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Set known-friends play as the default
  2. Confirm new friends with an adult
  3. Refuse cross-app gifts and trades
  4. Mute abusive chat without answering
  5. Report abusive players through the game's tools

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. Use and limits. The guard is a practice, not a review of any game's moderation, and parents should learn each game's specific settings with the child. title: Signature Video Choice Map
body:
The Signature Video Choice Map is Manon's original design for a map children draw of their video choices: what to watch, what to skip, and when to stop and tell an adult. The map's premise is that autoplay removes choice, and a child with a map chooses deliberately, because the map restores the moment autoplay took away.

The design exists because choice is the skill, and autoplay is the skill's enemy.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature video-choice map for children. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Draw a choice map: watch, skip, stop-and-tell
  2. Choose videos deliberately instead of following autoplay
  3. Turn on child or restricted settings where offered
  4. Learn that recommendations are system guesses, not personal advice
  5. Watch together sometimes and discuss choices

title: Signature Stop-Save-Tell Card
body:
The Signature Stop-Save-Tell Card is Manon's original design for a card a child can carry in memory: stop, save, tell. Stop means no angry reply. Save means keep messages with sender and date visible. Tell means show a trusted adult at once, and keep telling until someone acts. Its premise is that a child under attack cannot improvise, so the response must be three words long.

The design treats brevity as the feature: three words survive stress, while a manual does not.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature cyberbullying card for children. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Stop: send no angry reply
  2. Save: keep messages with sender and date visible
  3. Tell: show a trusted adult at once
  4. Block after saving, through the service's tools
  5. Keep telling until an adult acts

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: No angry reply; OK :: Messages saved; OK :: Adult told; OK :: Blocked after saving; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The card covers peer bullying response, not bullying involving threats, images, or persistent harassment, which need prompt adult, school, and where appropriate authority involvement. It does not replace counseling where harm has occurred. A common mistake is replying in anger or deleting the messages. title: Signature Purchase Pause
body:
The Signature Purchase Pause is Manon's original design for a pause before any in-game or in-app purchase: the child asks an adult, the adult approves or refuses, and every purchase is reviewed together afterwards. Its premise is that games make spending feel like playing, so the pause must be a rule set before play, when money still looks like money.

The design exists because a purchase approved during play is a purchase approved by excitement, not by judgment.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature purchase pause for children. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Require an adult's approval for every purchase
  2. Refuse offers demanding speed or secrecy
  3. Treat detail-seeking free items as purchases
  4. Review every purchase together afterwards
  5. Turn on purchase approval controls

title: Signature Readiness Ladder
body:
The Signature Readiness Ladder is Manon's original design for a ladder climbed rung by rung before a first social account: privacy settings demonstrated, stranger response demonstrated, pressure and comparison discussed, reporting demonstrated, and the account's purpose agreed. Its premise is that readiness is demonstrated, not dated, and a rung skipped is a rung that fails later.

The design replaces a birthday with evidence: a child climbs when the child shows the skill.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature social-media readiness ladder. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Demonstrate privacy settings on a practice account
  2. Demonstrate stranger response without prompting
  3. Discuss pressure, comparison, and curated feeds
  4. Demonstrate reporting and blocking unaided
  5. Agree the account's purpose and audience together

title: Signature Dare-Check
body:
The Signature Dare-Check is Manon's original design for a check before any dare: is it dangerous, humiliating, or illegal, and would a friend ask it if they knew the risk. The check comes with a ready refusal phrase practiced aloud, a private exit from harmful group chats, and a trusted adult who can be blamed for the refusal. Its premise is that refusal is a skill built by practice, not a trait summoned by lecture.

The design treats practice as the mechanism, because phrases practiced aloud are phrases available under pressure.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature peer-pressure dare-check. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Learn a short refusal phrase needing no argument
  2. Practice it aloud before it is needed
  3. Leave harmful group chats without announcement if needed
  4. Use a trusted adult as the reason when helpful
  5. Tell an adult when a dare involves danger or humiliation

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Refusal phrase learned; OK :: Refusal practiced aloud; OK :: Harmful chats exited; OK :: Dangerous dares reported; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The dare-check covers ordinary peer pressure, not dangerous challenges, which need immediate adult involvement and must never be attempted to prove a point. It does not replace counseling where harm has occurred. A common mistake is believing a dare from a friend is safer than the same dare from a stranger. title: Signature Family Response Plan
body:
The Signature Family Response Plan is Manon's original design for a plan written before trouble: who the child tells first, how evidence is saved, which adult contacts the school or service, and the promise that telling never brings punishment for telling. Its premise is that a plan rehearsed calmly is followed under stress, while a plan invented during a crisis is not a plan.

The design gives frightened children and worried parents the same next step, written down in advance.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature family response plan. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Name a first tell-person and a second if the first is unavailable
  2. Agree how evidence is saved before blocking
  3. Agree which adult contacts school or service
  4. Promise no punishment for telling
  5. Rehearse once calmly and fix gaps found

Use and limits. The plan handles ordinary incidents, not serious harm, illegal material, or threats, which need prompt professional and authority involvement. title: Signature Little-Helper Badge
body:
The Signature Little-Helper Badge is Manon's original design for older children who teach younger siblings: show one habit, watch the younger child try it, praise the attempt, and report difficulties to a parent. The badge is earned by teaching, not by supervising, and its premise is that teaching deepens the teacher's own knowledge while giving the younger child a teacher they will listen to.

The design treats teaching as the best test of understanding, and a sibling as the teacher most likely to be heard.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature sibling-teaching badge. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Show one habit on the younger child's own device
  2. Watch the younger child try it and praise the attempt
  3. Correct gently and show again without taking over
  4. Report difficulties to a parent
  5. Celebrate when the younger child teaches it back

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: One habit shown; OK :: Younger child tried it; OK :: Attempt praised; OK :: Difficulties reported to parent; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The badge supports but never replaces parental supervision, and where a younger child faces a serious problem, the older child must tell an adult at once, with no investigative role assigned. A common mistake is making the older child responsible for a younger child's safety, which is an adult's job. title: Signature Freedom Steps
body:
The Signature Freedom Steps is Manon's original design for freedoms granted as steps, not as a flood: supervised use, then independent use with checks, then a first account with agreed limits, then wider freedoms with reviews. Each step is earned by demonstrated practice and can be paused without shame. Its premise is that freedom practiced gradually is freedom handled well, while freedom granted all at once is freedom nobody has practiced.

The design replaces a birthday flood with a staircase, where each step is stood on before the next is taken.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach the child before restricting the child, because a rule a child understands is kept when no adult is watching; never shame a child for reporting, because shame is what keeps the next report from coming; and give freedoms gradually, earned by practice, not by age alone.

The working method is Signature graduated-freedom steps. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Define the next freedom clearly before granting it
  2. Grant it only after earlier habits are demonstrated
  3. Review it together after an agreed period
  4. Pause it without shame if it proves too much
  5. Celebrate each step handled well

Use and limits. The steps are a family judgment, not a schedule, and they must respect platform age limits and school rules. They do not cover independence in other areas of life. A common mistake is granting every freedom at once, then removing them all after the first problem.
